test_plan.scope: Validate FR-016..FR-029 (threshold-aware metric line, friendly subject, fire/resolve templates, elapsed-or-timestamp, systemd surface block, docker surface block, trend hint, deep-link footer, storm protection, MarkdownV2 escape, Test button, email parity, 4096-char cap, probable-cause line) plus NFR-005..NFR-009 (perf, reliability/fallback, observability, subprocess security, CI coverage). NFR-010 is declared not-applicable in requirements.
test_plan.approach: Three-layer pyramid. (1) Unit tests dominate — the renderer (internal/notify/render), markdown escaper (internal/notify/markdown), storm cache (internal/notify/storm), and probable-cause helpers (internal/notify/cause) are pure or near-pure and tested with golden files + table-driven cases + fuzz tests. (2) Integration tests exercise the dispatcher path with a stubbed Telegram API (httptest.Server intercepting api.telegram.org) and a real in-memory SQLite for AlertConfig lookups; these prove the wiring (engine→dispatcher→render→sender) end-to-end inside one process. (3) e2e tests exercise the 'Test Telegram' button via the existing /settings/telegram/test endpoint with a Playwright-driven settings page and a real test bot reaching a real test chat (same pattern as existing TestTelegram_*).
fixtures: newTestDispatcher(t) — builds Dispatcher with a stub Telegram HTTP server, stub SMTP server (smtptest), in-memory SQLite seeded via existing seedAlertConfig helper, fixed clock now=2026-05-07T10:00:00Z, hostname='ultron'
stubTelegramServer(t) — httptest.Server matching /bot<token>/sendMessage and /bot<token>/editMessageText; records every request body; returns configurable status+JSON
fakeJournalctl(t, lines []string, exitCode int) — replaces exec.Command in cause/journal.go via injectable execFn; t.Cleanup restores
fakeDockerLogs(t, lines []string, exitCode int) — same pattern for cause/docker.go
fakeProcSnapshot(t, top []ProcSample) — replaces /proc reader with an in-memory list of (comm, cpuPct, rssMB)
newRenderInput(t, opts ...) — builds a baseline RenderInput for resource-CPU fire; opts override individual fields (Cause, Trend, Surface, Kind=resolve, etc.)
loadGolden(t, name) — reads testdata/<name>.golden.txt; if -update flag set, writes the actual to that file
envSet(t, k, v) — sets env var, t.Cleanup unsets
playwrightCtx(t) — Playwright browser context logged in as test admin, settings page open
test_plan.exit_criteria: All TCs pass on linux/arm64 via `make verify`. Renderer benchmark BenchmarkRenderTelegramAlert reports p95 ≤ 50 ms. No new third-party Go dependency added (verified by `go list -m all` diff). Telegram MarkdownV2 fuzz test runs ≥10000 iterations without producing a body that fails Telegram's grammar validator. Integration coverage of internal/notify package ≥ pre-feature baseline (captured at start of phase 4).

test_cases.title: Static analysis: no exec.Command("sh", "-c", ...) in internal/notify/ (NFR-008)
test_cases.given: All .go files under internal/notify/
test_cases.when: Test parses each file and walks the AST
test_cases.then: No CallExpr to os/exec.Command whose first argument is the literal 'sh' or contains '-c' as any argument; no Command call with a single concatenated string-literal argument list
test_cases.expected_result: Subprocess invocations are argv-only

test_cases.title: Malicious unit name 'nginx; rm -rf /' is rejected before exec; renderer outputs 'invalid unit name' (NFR-008)
test_cases.given: Surface.Unit='nginx; rm -rf /'
test_cases.then: Function returns (*Cause)(nil) with no error; no subprocess is spawned (verified by assertExecCommandNotCalled); render output contains 'invalid unit name'
test_cases.expected_result: Allow-list regex catches injection attempts before they reach the kernel

test_cases.title: Container name with shell metacharacters '$(reboot)' rejected; no exec spawned (NFR-008)
test_cases.given: Surface.Container='$(reboot)'
test_cases.then: Returns (nil,nil); no subprocess spawned; render output for that block contains 'invalid container name'
test_cases.expected_result: Container-name allow-list enforced

test_cases.title: /proc reader rejects non-numeric pid string (NFR-008)

test_cases.then: Function returns error; no os.Open call is made on a path containing '..'; render omits the cause line
test_cases.expected_result: Path-traversal not possible via cause-derivation surface
